title: Tide and Songbook
premise: Theo Nakamura keeps her grandmother's lighthouse, a bakery lease she can barely afford, and a novel she's too afraid to finish. When the coastal town's anonymous pen-pal program pairs her with Jonah Reyes—the rival baker whose family lease is squeezing hers out—neither realizes who they're writing to, and both find themselves confessing truths they'd never say aloud. As the letters deepen and their daytime rivalry sharpens, Theo must choose between the safe invisibility she's built and the vulnerable, visible life Jonah's honesty demands. The story ends when the last train of the season leaves without one of them aboard: Jonah stays, they reveal their identities at the lighthouse, and together they sign a shared lease that turns two failing bakeries into one.
about_author: Rosalind Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes love stories about people who mistake solitude for safety, and still answers real letters by hand.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Twelve years after a fire took her parents' bakery and her mother's voice on the phone, Theo counts what remains: the lighthouse, a failing lease, forty pages of an unfinished novel. When the town librarian announces an anonymous winter pen-pal program, Theo signs up on impulse. Emotional beat: restless loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Flour Against Salt
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah Reyes returns to Harborline to save his father's bakery from the same landlord squeezing Theo out, though he doesn't know her name yet. He resents the town that watched his family struggle and signs up for the pen-pal program to prove he doesn't need anyone. Emotional beat: guarded pride curdling into isolation.

chapters.title: First Letter, No Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The first anonymous letters arrive: Theo writes about the lighthouse light she keeps burning; Jonah writes about bread his father taught him to shape by feel. Neither knows the other is the person they pass daily with narrowed eyes. Emotional beat: cautious wonder at being truly read.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out in Spring
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers the landlord intends to consolidate the two bakery spaces into one unit—a death sentence for whichever tenant blinks first. She and Jonah clash publicly at the harbor market. That night she tells her pen pal things she'd never tell him. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into combativeness.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah finds Theo's burned recipe book at a flea market and recognizes his own father's handwriting in its margins—their families were friends before the rivalry. He mails it anonymously to his pen pal instead of returning it to Theo directly. Emotional beat: guilt over a kindness he can't claim.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Holding the returned recipe book, Theo begins writing again—both the novel and braver letters. Her pen pal challenges her: 'Invisible isn't the same as safe.' Meanwhile Jonah offers, coldly, to buy out her lease 'for her own good.' Emotional beat: the sting of charity from someone who doesn't see her.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Bread
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A town bake-off forces Theo and Jonah onto the same stage; the tension between them reads as chemistry to everyone watching. That night, each writes their pen pal about the other—Theo complaining, Jonah defending her. Emotional beat: the irony of intimacy growing through complaint.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Chapter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo sends her pen pal the unfinished final chapter of her novel, in which a keeper lets the light go dark on purpose. Jonah reads it and realizes the prose echoes something familiar—but can't place it. Emotional beat: exposure without knowing you've been seen.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A winter storm knocks out the harbor road; Jonah shelters at the lighthouse when his delivery van fails. They talk for hours without the armor of daylight—almost honest, almost kind. He nearly tells her about the letters. Emotional beat: proximity making secrecy heavier.

chapters.title: Almost Told
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After the storm night, Theo catches herself looking for Jonah across the market. Her pen pal asks pointed questions about him, and she realizes she's describing someone she might love. Then the landlord serves formal eviction papers—on her, not him. Emotional beat: hope and betrayal arriving in the same envelope.

chapters.title: The Pen-Pal Reveal Rumor
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The librarian hints that identities will be revealed at the winter festival. Jonah panics: if Theo learns he's her pen pal after serving eviction papers, she'll read every letter as manipulation. He drafts a confession and burns it. Emotional beat: cowardice dressed up as protection.

chapters.title: Letters as Evidence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds a draft of Jonah's handwriting in the bakery's shared supply order book—matching her pen pal's script. She confronts nothing, but stops writing, and the silence devastates them both. Emotional beat: the specific grief of suspecting a kindness was strategy.

chapters.title: Dark Harbor
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. With Theo not answering, Jonah rereads all her letters and finally understands: she wasn't fragile, she was rebuilding. He goes to the lighthouse to apologize for the eviction papers—he signed as witness to protect his father's claim—and finds the light unlit and Theo gone. Emotional beat: dread that history is repeating itself.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Beaten, Theo books a one-way ticket on the last train of the season and packs the recipe book. But she leaves one final letter with the librarian to deliver to her pen pal: the truth about the fire, her mother, and why she let the light go dark in her novel. Emotional beat: farewell as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Confession at the Counter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The librarian gives Jonah Theo's letter. Reading it, he understands everything—including that she knows who he is. He runs to the station through sleet, misses the platform by seconds, and stands watching the empty track. Emotional beat: loss as the price of hesitation.

chapters.title: What Stays After the Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah doesn't board any train himself; instead he spends the night writing one long letter and taping it to the lighthouse door. Theo, stranded overnight by a canceled connection, comes home to find it. Emotional beat: choosing to stay made literal.

chapters.title: Everything I Didn't Sign
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reads Jonah's letter: the truth about the eviction, his father's debt, and the sentence that undoes her—'I would rather lose the bakery than be your stranger.' She climbs the tower and relights the lamp herself. Emotional beat: anger dissolving into the risk of belief.

chapters.title: The Festival Reveal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the winter festival, the librarian reveals pen-pal pairs publicly. Theo and Jonah stand before the town already knowing, and instead of humiliation there's applause—and the landlord, shamed by the crowd, offers renegotiation. Emotional beat: visibility chosen, not forced.

chapters.title: One Lease, Two Names
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah proposes merging the bakeries under a single lease bearing both names—his father's recipes and hers, side by side. His father resists; Theo's grandmother's logbook convinces him the families were partners once before. Emotional beat: legacy reinterpreted as inheritance rather than debt.

chapters.title: The Finished Chapter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finishes her novel and reads the last chapter aloud at the reopened bakery: a keeper who lets the light go dark so the town will learn to light its own. Jonah hears his own story in it. Emotional beat: art as the truest confession.

chapters.title: Tide Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First morning of the merged bakery: flour and salt, two ovens, one counter. They exchange letters one last time—read aloud, face to face, no anonymity left. Emotional beat: intimacy surviving the loss of distance.

chapters.title: Keepers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. One year later: the lighthouse automated, the bakery thriving, a new pen-pal season beginning with Theo as its organizer. On the door, a sign in two hands: 'Open until the last train leaves—and after.' Emotional beat: memory honored, identity claimed, home chosen.
